newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close up, led by blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close up, led by blue chips.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks, which closed higher on gains in expensive blue chips, were restrained by profit-taking among cheap counters, brokers said.

The all share index closed 14.4 points up at 721.2. Price gains led declines by 52 to 37. Development Finance rose 15 rupees to 275, John Keells Holdings 10 to 229, Hatton National 32.75 to 293, National Development Bank 25 to 235, Lanka Orix Leasing 22.75 to 180.
"The rising number of price declines shows profit-taking is on the increase as the index has gained over 70 points in the last two weeks," said Sanjeeva Gunewardena of Ceylinco Stock Brokers.

The index has risen on the back of improved investor sentiment due to a cut in reserve ratios, easing interest rates, a sweeping election win by the government and its agreement with the opposition to work together to end the ethnic crisis, brokers said.
Turnover was 165.6 million rupees on 5.7 million shares, led by 125,000 shares of Aitken Spence, 1.6 million Asian Hotels, 50,000 Commercial Bank, 50,000 Hayleys and 100,000 Lanka Orix Leasing.
"The market should enter a phase of consolidation next week as more profit-taking sets in," said Deva Ellpola, of brokerage Jardine Fleming.
